gloss: freshly made; just finished; hot out of the oven

definitions.gloss: freshly made; just finished; brand new
definitions.explanation: describes something that has just been made, prepared, or completed, emphasizing its newness and freshness

examples.japanese: {出来立|できた}てのパンはおいしい。
{出来立|できた}ての{料理|りょうり}を{温|あたた}かいうちに{食|た}べよう。
examples.english: Let's eat the freshly made food while it's still warm.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}では{出来立|できた}てのピザが{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: At this restaurant, you can eat freshly made pizza.

notes:
FORMATION:
{出来|でき}る (to be done, completed) + {立|た}て (just after ~ing) → just after being made

FUNCTIONS AS:
- Noun: {出来立|できた}てが{一番|いちばん} (freshly made is best)
- No-adjective: {出来立|できた}ての{料理|りょうり} (freshly made dish)

THE ～{立|た}て PATTERN:
This suffix indicates "just after doing something." Common examples:
- {焼|や}き{立|た}て (freshly baked)
- {揚|あ}げ{立|た}て (freshly fried)
- {茹|ゆ}で{立|た}て (freshly boiled)
- {炊|た}き{立|た}て (freshly cooked - rice)
- {採|と}れ{立|た}て (freshly picked/harvested)

USAGE:
Often used in food contexts to emphasize freshness and quality. Restaurants may advertise {出来立|できた}て{提供|ていきょう} (served freshly made) as a selling point.
